Amortize PME atom-grid re-sort for large systems (#5305)

Large systems (>15000 atoms) re-sorted the PME atom grid every step,
skipping the step-counter amortization used for smaller systems. On
current GPUs the per-step sort is mostly wasted work, so re-sort every
2 steps instead. Smaller systems are unchanged. The sort only changes
charge-spread memory locality; results are identical up to floating-point
summation order.

Add computeStressTensor() to MonteCarloFlexibleBarostat. (#5322)

* Add computeStressTensor() to MonteCarloFlexibleBarostat. This adds a new finite-difference stress-tensor API that applies a consistent strain to both the atomic coordinates and box vectors, while leaving computeCurrentPressure() unchanged. It also adds a triclinic regression test, Python unit metadata, and user-guide/API documentation.

* Use scaleCoordinates() for computeStressTensor() and add independent tests.

Extend scaleCoordinates() with optional shear factors so the stress tensor finite difference runs entirely on the GPU instead of downloading, deforming, and re-uploading coordinates.
The three new shear arguments default to zero, so all existing barostats are unchanged.
Add an analytic two-particle harmonic bond test and a LAMMPS cross-validation test (hardcoded reference values) as independent checks of computeStressTensor().

* Fix computeStressTensor() on GPU platforms by deforming coordinates continuously. Saving and restoring the coordinates around each finite difference energy evaluation produced an inaccurate energy on the CUDA/OpenCL platforms. computeStressComponent() now applies the strain continuously (forward, then to the opposite strain, then back), mimicking computePressureComponent().

* Add a test for computeStressTensor() with includeKinetic=true, validated against the full (virial + kinetic) pressure tensor from LAMMPS.

* Add missing @param tags for scaleCoordinates shear arguments

resize-on-overflow logic never triggers, leaving both vectors empty;
operator[] on an empty vector is undefined behavior even though the
resulting address is only used to satisfy an iNumNeighbors == 0 range
that the caller never dereferences.

This is silently tolerated by an ordinary -O3 -DNDEBUG build but
reliably aborts under libstdc++'s _GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS hardening
(confirmed via gdb backtraces landing exactly on this call site: with
Assertion '__n < this->size()' failed). Use .data(), which is
well-defined for pointer arithmetic on an empty vector, instead of
operator[]/&vec[i].

* Fix undefined behavior from operator[] in CpuConstantPotentialForce

Several call sites relied on operator[] to take an address rather
than to read a value, which is undefined behavior in two distinct
ways that both showed up under libstdc++'s _GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS
hardening (confirmed via gdb):

- initialize() cached exclusions/sysToElec/elecToSys/sysElec/elecElec/
  electrodeParams as &vec[0]. These vectors can legitimately be empty
  (e.g. elecToSys and elecElec when numElectrodeParticles == 0), and
  every later use of the resulting pointers is already guarded by a
  loop bounded by the matching count, so the address is computed but
  never dereferenced in that case -- still undefined behavior via
  operator[] regardless.

- solveImpl(), ensureValid(), and getDerivativesThread() used
  &vec[0]/&vec[n] as a one-past-end pointer for assign(begin, end)
  calls and similar. operator[] is only defined for indices < size(),
  so &vec[n] is undefined behavior on *every* call, not only when the
  vector is empty: confirmed aborting with an ordinary non-empty
  vector (numElectrodeParticles == chargeDerivatives.size() == 2).

Both are silently tolerated by an ordinary -O3 -DNDEBUG build. Where
the consumer needs an actual pointer (cached member fields, the
CpuConstantPotentialPmeIO constructor), use .data(), which is
well-defined for pointer arithmetic up to and including size(). The
four assign() calls in solveImpl() take a templated iterator pair
rather than requiring pointers, and chargeDerivatives is always
resized to numElectrodeParticles in initialize(), well before
solveImpl() ever runs, so those use .begin()/.end() directly instead
of recomputing the same range via pointer arithmetic; an assert right
after the first getDerivatives() call documents and checks that
size-invariant for anyone changing initialize()/update() later,
though like the -O3 -DNDEBUG case above it only holds in debug/
assert-enabled builds.

Remove stray shebangs and normalize CRLF line endings in unit/ modules (#5356)

These openmm.unit and amber_file_parser modules are library code, never
meant to be run directly, but eleven of them carried a "#!/bin/env
python" shebang despite shipping without the executable bit set.
doctests.py additionally had Windows-style CRLF line endings throughout
the file, unlike the rest of the codebase. Neither affects Python
import/execution, but both are packaging-lint failures for any
downstream (e.g. rpmlint's non-executable-script and
wrong-script-end-of-line-encoding checks) and are simple to fix at the
source.

Co-authored-by: Vedran Miletić <vedran.miletic@mpcdf.mpg.de>

Support building the Python extension against a DESTDIR-staged install (#5358)

setup.py links openmm._openmm against OPENMM_LIB_PATH, which is always
the final, real installation directory -- correct for the runtime
rpath, but wrong as the linker's search path in any packaging workflow
that stages a build into a temporary root (DESTDIR) before the real
system install, since the just-built C++ libraries only exist under
DESTDIR + OPENMM_LIB_PATH at that point, not OPENMM_LIB_PATH itself.
This is the normal pattern used by most Linux distro packaging (RPM,
deb, etc.) via "make install DESTDIR=...", and currently fails there
with "cannot find -lOpenMM" (confirmed with a from-scratch build).

Search DESTDIR + OPENMM_LIB_PATH (empty DESTDIR is a no-op, so this is
unchanged when not building via a staged install) while leaving the
extension's runtime_library_dirs -- and the existing Darwin -rpath,
which already did this correctly -- pointing at the clean
OPENMM_LIB_PATH, since DESTDIR never exists on the system the
extension actually runs on.

Verified with a full two-pass DESTDIR build (matching the pattern
OpenMM's own docs describe: build+install the C++ libraries, then
build the Python wrapper referencing the now-installed libraries):
fails with "cannot find -lOpenMM" without this change, builds and
installs cleanly with it, and the resulting extension's RUNPATH
correctly points at the real (non-DESTDIR) OPENMM_LIB_PATH either way.
